_doc: Known-answer case registry for the Phase-1 benchmark gate (see DESIGN.md, BENCHMARK.md). All paths repo-relative. Published numbers transcribed from on-disk ground truth (HEPData YAML + arXiv LaTeX source); each value cites its source in published.sources/notes. cases[].required tiers + mu95 baselines are LOCKED to the 2026-06-09 measured baseline (regression semantics); relax only deliberately via a reviewed commit. sigma_scale_k here is the ONLY k-factor authority for a case (the C1N2 run's on-disk nlo_xsec.json k=0.421 is a known single-charge artifact - never read k from run dirs).

tier_ladders._doc: Benchmark scoring ladders (distinct from the cert engines' internal driving/contributing tolerances). axe: |ratio-1| of the driving-SR acc*eff vs published grid. limit: symmetric deviation max(r,1/r)-1 of our driving-SR s95 (events) vs the published model-independent S95 (arXiv:1605.03814-style Table 6); 'within 2x' = 1.0.

published.notes: REGISTERED AGAINST A RUN-LOCAL PATCHED ROUTINE (policy precedent from ins2016_conf_2016_037's case, registrar-owned): the installed share ATLAS_2022_I2182381.cc unconditionally calls getONNX(name()) in init(), but upstream Rivet (gitlab.com/hepcedar/rivet, analyses/pluginONNX/) ships this routine's .cc/.info/.plot WITHOUT the matching .onnx weight file -- confirmed absent both in the installed rivet 4.1.3 conda package and in the upstream repo tree (GitLab API tree listing of analyses/pluginONNX/, 2026-07-08) -- so the routine cannot init() at all, let alone run, as shipped, for ANY user. Patch (config/rivet_patched/ATLAS_2022_I2182381_PATCHED.cc, share untouched, RIVET_ANALYSIS_PATH override) removes ONLY the ONNX load + the entirely-NN-scoped analyze() block; a full source read confirms the removed code never sets a variable the CC (cut-and-count) block reads and contains no vetoEvent, so every CC SR yield (SR_Gbb_0l_{B,M,C}, this case's registered family) is bit-for-bit unaffected by the removal. Upstream Rivet report recommended (missing data file, not a logic defect). MACHINERY: pairing_check.py PASS on all 3 regions; pyhf_exclude.py likelihood (Mode A) EXCLUDED all 3 (mu95_obs NLO: B=0.174, M=0.245, C=0.299); counting-mode reconstruction of the driving SR (B) agrees with Mode A to 1.5% (obs) / 4.8% (exp) -- see RESULT.md. CERT: axe_tier=Acceptable (driving SR_Gbb_0l_B ratio=1.265, all 3 CC regions high by a consistent 24-27%), cert-engine strict verdict FAIL (driving-SR rule tolerance is 12-15% per .claude/rules/statistics.md; this case's 26.5% residual EXCEEDS it by ~2x -- "Acceptable" here means the benchmark's own looser 3-tier scoring ladder (<=30%), a LOOSER bar than the strict driving-SR rule, not equivalent to it). HONEST RELABEL (adversarial-review correction, supersedes the original fast-sim-floor attribution): 26.5% EXCEEDS the intrinsic ~10-20% fast-sim+LO floor, so "fast-sim-floor" undersold it; better-attributed cause = b-tag-efficiency offset (~8%/b-tag compounded over 3 required b-tags, (1.08)^3=1.26, matching the observed 1.265 ratio), ABOVE the nominal fast-sim floor, UNCERTIFIED (plausibility-matched, not measured against a control sample). Bias direction makes our limit too tight, so correcting it only weakens the limit TOWARD the published value -- verdict-robust: our predicted NLO+NNLL signal sigma (1.709 fb) exceeds ATLAS's own published sigma-UL (0.413 fb) at this node by ~4.1x, so the EXCLUDED verdict holds even checked directly against the paper's own limit, independent of this attribution being exactly right. informational sigma-UL check: our Mode-A sigma-UL(obs,NLO)=0.298 fb vs published 0.413 fb (28% tighter, consistent in direction+magnitude with the A*eps excess). No model-independent S95(events) table exists for this analysis -> limit_tier null (informational sigma_ul_tier_info only), matching the ins1676551(C1N2) case's precedent for the same reason. GATE-VS-LIKELIHOOD CAVEAT (adversarial-review correction): run_benchmark.py has no pyhf_mode="likelihood" hook, so this case is regression-gated via required.mu95_stability.baseline_mu95_obs=0.17694018928599856, the COUNTING-mode reconstruction (outputs/counting/exclusion.json), NOT a live pyhf-likelihood re-run of the Mode-A workspaces -- the Mode-A obs_limit itself is 0.17428109495495014 (outputs/likelihood_B/exclusion.json), agreeing with the counting proxy to +1.53%. The gate therefore verifies the counting proxy stays stable, not that the Mode-A likelihood machinery stays correct; tracked as CR-044 (docs/development/change-registry.md, OPEN/DEFERRED) to add a real pyhf_mode="likelihood" hook before this case is treated as gate-verified at the Mode-A level.
